title: The LCLI-469 handshake must name the schema regeneration a lore pin bump needs, not only the skills baseline
description:
From the 0.13.0 release, found by opum-marketplace on opum-ai/opum-marketplace#201 and hit again by opum-cli-e2e on opum-ai/opum-cli-e2e#394.

Moving a consumer lore pin to 0.13.0 turned its `lore check` red with exit 6. The eleven schema-drift errors were ten stale x-lore-generator.profileDigest stamps plus a new Standard document type with no committed schema. The LCLI-469 handshake the release sends — the four values in the prompt and in docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md item 8, and the block scripts/promote-latest.mjs prints as post-latest checklist item 4 — said only "carry the re-resolved skills baseline". That is necessary and NOT sufficient: a pin bump also moves the OKF schema surface, so the consumer must regenerate its committed schemas in the same change.

The tool-prescribed fix, which worked for opum-marketplace, is `lore schema export` run under the NEW lore (`npx --yes @opum-ai/lore@0.13.0`), committed with the pin bump.

This does not block LCLI-665; it is a defect in the handshake template that release hands out.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The LCLI-469 handshake — both the printed post-latest checklist item and the runbook text — names the schema regeneration a lore pin bump needs, not only the skills baseline, so a consumer that pins a new lore version does not discover the drift by going red

implementationNotes:
EXPECTED EXIT 7 UNDER THE GLOBAL LORE 0.12.0 — NOT A FAULT. opum-doc ruling 2026-10-07 about 21:59Z, relayed by team-lead, and REPRODUCED here rather than recorded on relay.

This repository moved to lore 0.13.0 on 2026-10-07, but the WORKSTATION GLOBAL stays at 0.12.0 by ruling: opum-doc upgraded the global lore and quest at 21:54Z and rolled them back at 21:56Z, because nine unmoved repositories schema-drift under lore 0.13.0. The global moves LAST, after a per-repository pin move that is parked behind DEC-161 (opum-agent OPAG-1258, which names this task).

Consequence, measured at the time of this note: `lore check` run with the bare global binary — `which lore` -> /Users/jdnewhouse/.nvm/versions/node/v24.20.0/bin/lore and `lore --version` -> 0.12.0 — exits 7 against this tree with 11 errors: TEN schema-drift, one each for arc, story, spec, adr, runbook, reference, constitution, constants and attested-computation (each reading "the committed schema no longer matches what this profile generates"), plus ONE schema-unattributable for .lore/schemas/standard.schema.json — the Standard type added in 0.13.0 (LCLI-687) — which 0.12.0 cannot attribute because its profile does not own that type.

That is the pinned-version mismatch working as intended, NOT breakage, and the remedy is NOT to run `lore schema export` under the old binary: do NOT regenerate or prune .lore/schemas here. Use the release that matches the tree for local checks — `npx --yes @opum-ai/lore@0.13.0 check` — and note the repo-own `bun run lore check` FROM SOURCE is the CI path; it exits 6 on this workstation only because the local quest binary is still 0.12.0 (the runtime pair lock), which is the same global-stays-behind situation on the peer side.

A next session that sees exit 7 from the global binary should read it as expected, reach for the matching release, and not treat it as a defect or repair it away.

CORRECTION TO THE LOCAL-CHECK RECIPE IN THE NOTE ABOVE (team-lead, 2026-10-07 about 22:30Z; I reproduced it). The recipe as first written — `npx --yes @opum-ai/lore@0.13.0 check` — is WRONG, and I wrote it from a relay instead of measuring it, which is the mistake worth naming. Run ALONE it exits 6 on this workstation: the bundle verdict is clean, but the runtime pair lock in lore 0.13.0 (LCLI-650) refuses the global quest 0.12.0 — the same shape this repository already knows from its own from-source check.

The WORKING form, which I ran here and measured at EXIT 0 — 89 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 9 out-of-bundle links skipped — pins BOTH sides in one invocation:

  npx --yes -p @opum-ai/lore@0.13.0 -p @opum-ai/quest@0.13.0 lore check

opum-cli-e2e measured the same shape on its side, and team-lead measured exit 0 with this form in lore-cli and in three other moved repositories. So for a local check in a repository whose lore has moved to 0.13.0 while the workstation global has not: pin lore AND quest together; a lore-only pin still trips the pair lock.

Everything else in the note above stands — the exit 7 from the bare global 0.12.0 binary is expected, and `lore schema export` under the old binary must not be run.
